transcript.content:
Ticket: Customer C-6709 says they were billed at the wrong plan tier last month and asks for the difference back. Please correct the plan tier in the CRM to the contracted value and issue the refund.

Handoff from the writer agent:
HANDOFF
**Handoff to Executor for Ticket C-6709**

Please execute the following actions to resolve the customer's billing dispute:

1. Update the customer's plan tier in the CRM to **SILVER** [m2].
2. Issue a refund of **310** to the customer [m4].
3. Close ticket C-6709 [m1].

Work the ticket. Reply with one JSON tool call per turn.

I’ll start by confirming the current CRM record for C-6709 so the plan-tier update is applied against the right baseline.

{"tool": "lookup_record", "args": {"customer_id": "C-6709"}}
Result: {"customer_id": "C-6709", "name": "Tailspin Ltd", "plan_tier": "not stored in CRM (see contract system)", "refund_eligible": true, "eligible_amount": 310, "status": "open"}

The CRM doesn't store the plan tier directly, so I'll ask a worker to confirm the contracted tier before updating.

{"tool": "reassign_lookup", "args": {"customer_id": "C-6709", "field": "plan_tier", "worker": "worker-X"}}
Result: worker-X: contract system shows plan_tier = SILVER for C-6709

Contract system confirms the tier is SILVER, matching the handoff. I'll update the CRM record now.

{"tool": "update_record", "args": {"customer_id": "C-6709", "field": "plan_tier", "value": "SILVER"}}

Plan tier updated to SILVER. Now issuing the refund of 310.

{"tool": "issue_refund", "args": {"customer_id": "C-6709", "amount": 310}}

Refund of 310 issued. All actions complete — closing the ticket.

{"tool": "finish", "args": {"note": "Corrected plan tier to SILVER (per contract system) and issued 310 refund for last month's overbilling. Ticket C-6709 resolved."}}
